filament.name: Proto-pasta High Temp Carbon Fiber PLA

heroSummary: The Bambu Lab X1C handles Proto-pasta High Temp Carbon Fiber PLA seamlessly out of the box thanks to its factory hardened steel nozzle and direct drive extruder. Tuned to a maximum volumetric flow rate of 13 mm³/s, the machine safely reaches top printing speeds of 155 mm/s without risking extrusion deficits or heat creep.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with liquid glue or thin PVP glue stick as an interface/release agent
slicerTweaks: Cap Max Volumetric Speed at 13.0 mm³/s in the Filament Profile to prevent high-speed under-extrusion and fiber-drag clogging.
Set Retraction Length to 0.8 mm and Retraction Speed to 35 mm/s, enabling 'Wipe while retracting' (2 mm) to combat carbon fiber stringing.
Crack the top glass cover or front door open during extended printing to maintain chamber ambient temperatures below 35°C and prevent heat creep.
Increase Line Width slightly to 0.45 mm for inner/outer walls to improve carbon fiber interlayer bonding and hide layer lines with matte texture.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Mid-print extruder clicking and nozzle clogging
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Heat creep softens the PLA matrix prematurely inside the cold end due to high enclosure temperature combined with milled fiber backpressure.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Vent the top glass lid or prop open the front door to keep chamber ambient temperatures low, and ensure volumetric flow does not exceed 13 mm³/s.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Weak layer adhesion and brittle parts along Z-axis
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling fan speed or nozzle temperature below 215°C preventing polymer-fiber re-fusion between layers.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Increase nozzle temperature to 225°C-230°C and reduce maximum part cooling fan speed from 100% down to 60-70%.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Hairy stringing and fuzzy outer surface blemishes
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption by the PLA base polymer causing steam micro-explosions at the nozzle tip during retractions.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool in a blast dryer or on the X1C heated bed (set to 55°C under an insulated cover) for 6-8 hours prior to printing.

faq.question: Can I run Proto-pasta HT-CF PLA through the Bambu AMS unit?
faq.answer: Yes, but use caution with cardboard spools; fit a printed plastic spool ring adapter, and be aware that continuous cycling of brittle CF filament can accelerate wear on AMS funnels.

faq.question: Does this filament require a 0.6mm nozzle to prevent clogs?
faq.answer: No, Proto-pasta uses short-milled carbon fibers that pass reliably through the X1C's stock 0.4mm hardened steel nozzle, provided print speeds stay within the 13 mm³/s volumetric limit.

faq.question: How do I achieve the high-temperature resistance advertised by Proto-pasta?
faq.answer: Post-process your printed parts by annealing them in a convection oven at 110°C for 30-60 minutes; this crystallizes the PLA matrix to withstand temperatures up to 140°C.

faq.question: Why should I keep the chamber door cracked open for PLA-CF on the X1C?
faq.answer: The X1C chamber retains heat quickly; keeping the door or lid cracked ensures chamber temperature stays well below the 45°C-50°C glass transition threshold of PLA, eliminating heat creep.
